layer_b_event_mappings.example_market: "Will the Fed cut rates at the December meeting?"
layer_b_event_mappings.mechanism: A higher implied probability of a cut lowers expected front-end rates; duration is the sensitivity of a bond's price to that path, so long-duration Treasuries gain mechanically more than short-duration ones. Transmission is direct via the discount rate, not via earnings.
layer_b_event_mappings.beta_status: not_estimable_here: needs a matched time series of market-implied probabilities and bond returns; we hold neither, and inventing a number would breach the no-fabrication rule.

layer_b_event_mappings.mechanism: An inflation surprise raises the expected policy path and the inflation risk premium, pushing nominal yields up and bond prices down; TIPS reprice partly through the breakeven rather than the real rate, so the sign is smaller; gold responds to the real-rate component.
layer_b_event_mappings.expected_sign: probability(high CPI) up  =>  TLT down; TIP down less; GLD ambiguous
layer_b_event_mappings.beta_status: not_estimable_here: same missing series problem as the Fed row.

layer_b_event_mappings.example_market: "Will there be a US recession declared before 2027?"
layer_b_event_mappings.mechanism: Recession odds reprice the equity risk premium and the earnings path; defensive sectors (staples, utilities) have lower earnings beta to the cycle, so the long-short SPY vs XLP spread is the cleaner expression than SPY alone.
layer_b_event_mappings.expected_sign: probability(recession) up  =>  SPY down relative to XLP

layer_b_event_mappings.mechanism: A threshold market on the same underlying is a risk-neutral probability of the terminal price; it transmits to spot only through the same underlying, so it is a repricing of the same variable, not a leading indicator.
layer_b_event_mappings.expected_sign: probability(BTC > K) up  =>  BTC spot up
layer_b_event_mappings.beta_status: near-tautological: the market IS the underlying. A beta would mostly measure the market's own settlement, not a causal transmission.

layer_b_event_mappings.example_market: "Will the S&P 500 close above 6500 this year?"
layer_b_event_mappings.mechanism: Index level markets settle on the same index they reference, so the mapping is definitional. Useful as a crowd-priced scenario distribution; not an independent signal about the index.
layer_b_event_mappings.beta_status: not meaningful - definitional identity, not a transmission.

rules.layer_b: Every row carries a transmission mechanism, an expected sign and a confidence. A row without a mechanism is rejected in code.
